---
name: backlog-refinement
description: Refine feature ideas, bugs, and feedback into implementation-ready backlog items. Use when drafting or reviewing issues, acceptance criteria, scope, dependencies, priority, or backlog decomposition.
---

# Backlog Refinement

1. Search the repository and existing backlog for related behavior, prior decisions, duplicates, and dependencies.
2. Restate the user or business problem without assuming a solution.
3. Identify missing decisions. Ask only questions whose answers materially change scope or behavior.
4. Define scope and non-goals.
5. Write acceptance criteria as observable outcomes. Include negative and boundary behavior when relevant.
6. Record dependencies, risks, documentation needs, telemetry needs, and test notes.
7. Split work when items can be delivered and validated independently; preserve traceability between them.
8. Recommend priority from value, urgency, risk reduction, and effort, while labeling assumptions.

Use this issue shape:

```markdown
## Problem

## User or business value

## Scope

## Non-goals

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given ..., when ..., then ...

## Dependencies and risks

## Test notes

## Documentation notes

## Open questions
```

Before any GitHub write operation, show the proposed issue content and obtain approval.
